This bill would change which court hears challenges to migration decisions.
It would make the Migration Act treat certain types of decisions, including those that appear invalid, the same way for jurisdiction purposes.
The bill would also confirm that a range of administrative actions count as decisions for the Federal Circuit Court and Federal Court.
The bill would clarify that a migration decision includes decisions that appear to be outside the court's power.
It would extend the same treatment to decisions made under the Administrative Appeals Tribunal Act.
The bill would ensure that the Federal Circuit Court and Federal Court have consistent jurisdiction over these decisions.
People and organisations involved in migration cases, and the Federal Circuit Court and Federal Court.

The Migration Amendment (Clarification of Jurisdiction) Bill 2018 amends the Migration Act to clarify that all relevant migration decisions are subject to a uniform judicial review scheme, with first-instance challenges heard in the Federal Circuit Court. The bill responds to the Federal Court decision in *Minister for Immigration and Border Protection v ARJ 17*, which had excluded certain erroneous decisions from the definition of a migration decision.
